speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any specific triggers for your cough, such as exposure to dust, chemicals, or cold air? Also, have you noticed any wheezing or shortness of breath during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have a long history of recurrent bronchitis and copious purulent sputum as a non-smoker, have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for tuberculosis, or do you have any family history of this disease? REQUEST TEST: Tuberculin_skin_test.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No other significant past medical history aside from the recurrent bronchitis. Social history: Non-smoker, no history of alcohol or drug abuse.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, weight loss, night sweats, or shortness of breath. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: This patient's presentation of chronic cough with copious purulent sputum for 11 years is highly characteristic of Bronchiectasis; the previous suggestion of Pyelonephritis is incorrect as the symptoms do not involve urinary tract findings. I will request a Chest_X-Ray and Sputum_Culture to confirm the diagnosis and identify any underlying pathogens.
